futurists-and-foresight-practitioners-fu.headline: Futurists & Foresight Practitioners - Futures Thinking As Life Skill
futurists-and-foresight-practitioners-fu.author: Jacinta Robinson
futurists-and-foresight-practitioners-fu.core: Posted in last 7 days Futurists & Foresight Practitioners - Futures Thinking As Life Skill The more time I spend in strategic foresight and futures thinking, the more convinced I become that we're missing a huge opportunity to democratise the tools, techniques and practice. Why isn't this kind of structured thinking more widely taught and practised as an everyday life skill? Much of the work understandably focuses on government policy, national security and organisational strategy. I get it. That work matters, and I've spent much of my own career in those spaces. But I keep asking: what about everyone else? The SME owner making decisions about their next five years? The woman navigating midlife, career changes, financial pressures and caring responsibilities? Communities trying to understand how climate, technology and economic changes might affect their lives? Leaders making decisions amid so much change and uncertainty? We talk about climate change, technological disruption and economic uncertainty, alongside policy responses and individual responsibility. Yet we're overlooking something fundamental: people's ability to understand how decisions made today connect to the futures they're helping create. Individuals are the building blocks of change and society. Imagine more people able to recognise early signals of change, think critically about what they mean, explore plausible scenarios, challenge assumptions and understand their agency to influence what happens next. Imagine people making decisions with a longer-term view. Could this help address the short-term thinking of our 3–4 year voting cycles? SMEs designing businesses for the world they're moving into. Could that improve productivity and our economy? Leaders creating organisations with a genuine sense of the future they're working towards. The benefits could extend well beyond individuals. We'd have a society better equipped to navigate change and make intentional collective choices. So why aren't more of us taking foresight beyond traditional policy and organisational environments? I suspect part of the answer is that it's difficult to make a living doing this work with individuals. I've certainly discovered that over the past six months. Still, I'm committed. I genuinely believe strategic foresight is a life skill, and I want more people to have the opportunity to learn and practise it. This is something I want to explore through my podcast – See It. Shape It. Own It. I'm looking to connect with strategic foresight practitioners and futurists interested in joining me for conversations in 2027 about the changes shaping people's lives, futures thinking as a life skill, imagining better futures and intentional future design for individuals, SMEs, communities and leaders. If this resonates with you, I'd love to hear from you. You don't have to be a practitioner to have something valuable to contribute. Let's broaden the conversation.

By submitting, you're giving me permission to narrate and share your experience with listeners, potentially with minor edits for clarity, pacing, and storytelling while preserving the heart of your experience. Whilst losing your job and your income doesn't usually go hand in hand with being able to afford more trips to the theatre, I really want to use this extra free time as an opportunity to delve back into my love of content creation and chatting to creative people who have fascinating stories to tell. After all, it's how I landed my first job in journalism over five years ago - by working hard, voluntarily, on my very own regional radio show about women in the music industry. So, today, I made some fresh plans to cover some exciting upcoming news in the theatre industry and I'm thrilled to be able to document this journey, here on my LinkedIn. If you're a creative or a PR in the theatre space and you have a story I should be telling on my Instagram and TikTok pages (linked in the comments), I'd love to hear from you - please don't hesitate to pop me a message for my PR email address! P.S - this is me at the Royal Albert Hall seeing Sylvia the Musical on the weekend. It's a show about one of my favourite topics - suffrage - and I was even upgraded to a box, which felt right fancy 😆 #contentcreation #redundancy #theatreblogger #journalist #prrequest #journorequest
